title: Smart_object
summary:
The smart object concept was introduced by Marcelo Kallmann and Daniel Thalmann as an object that can describe its own possible interactions. The main focus is to model interactions of smart virtual objects with virtual humans or agents in virtual worlds. The additional information provided by this concept enables far more general interaction schemes and can greatly simplify the planner of an artificial intelligence agent. A smart object does not necessarily need to be intelligent as in exhibiting a strong essence of artificial intelligence, although it can be designed to also be intelligent.

Physical world smart objects can be described in terms of three properties: awareness, which is a smart object's ability to sense, interpret, and react to events and human activities; representation, which refers to a smart object's application and programming model; and interaction, which denotes the object's ability to converse with the user in terms of input, output, control, and feedback.

Activity-aware smart objects are objects that can record information about work activities and their own use. Policy-aware smart objects are activity-aware objects that can interpret events and activities with respect to predefined organizational policies. A smart object is an object that enhances the interaction with not only people but also with other smart objects. Also known as smart connected products or smart connected things, they are products, assets and other things embedded with processors, sensors, software and connectivity that allow data to be exchanged between the product and its environment, manufacturer, operator, and other products and systems.

More recently in the early 2010s, smart objects have been proposed as a key enabler for the vision of the Internet of Things. The Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) is the combination of AI technologies with IoT infrastructure to create systems capable of sensing, learning, and acting on data without continuous human intervention.
